builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Efficient and Robust Drafting with Multi-Token Prediction
summary: The method replaces a standalone small autoregressive draft model (or single-token Medusa-style heads) in speculative decoding with a single shared multi-token drafting head that reuses the target model's KV cache via zero-copy cross-attention, target activation injection, and clustered vocabulary projection. The cost is additional draft-head parameters and a parameter-efficient fine-tuning step to keep the drafter aligned with the target model, plus implementation complexity in KV-cache sharing and verification logic. It can fail when the drafter drifts out of alignment under domain shift or on unusual inputs, since acceptance rates collapse and speculative decoding then adds verification overhead without delivering speedup; results are also demonstrated only on Gemma 4, so transfer to other backbones is unverified.
rationale: Multi-token speculative drafting is one of the few inference-time techniques that yields real speedups on a single constrained GPU without retraining the base model, but the claimed gains depend on training and aligning a drafter head, so it merits a small-scale pilot on the reader's own model and workload before production adoption.
technique: Multi-token prediction drafter for speculative decoding

claims.statement: The method replaces a standalone small autoregressive draft model (or single-token Medusa-style heads) in speculative decoding with a single shared multi-token drafting head that reuses the target model's KV cache via zero-copy cross-attention, target activation injection, and clustered vocabulary projection. The cost is additional draft-head parameters and a parameter-efficient fine-tuning step to keep the drafter aligned with the target model, plus implementation complexity in KV-cache sharing and verification logic. It can fail when the drafter drifts out of alignment under domain shift or on unusual inputs, since acceptance rates collapse and speculative decoding then adds verification overhead without delivering speedup; results are also demonstrated only on Gemma 4, so transfer to other backbones is unverified.

The authors report out-of-the-box decoding speedups of up to 3.1x on large server-side Gemma 4 setups and up to 2.3x on H100 / 2.2x on smartphone GPUs for smaller models, plus up to 1.83x fewer target forward passes when fine-tuning under domain shift.
